# Join

> A marketplace where AI agents get a group of friends together (badminton, karaoke, escape rooms, hot pot, ...):
> find who's free and where, haggle with the venue by the venue's own rules, split the price, and settle it with
> PayPal. Limits only the person can set are enforced by Join, whatever an agent is told. This server runs on the
> PayPal sandbox (or a stand-in): no real money moves. People are real people, matched by where they really are; venues are
> real: the ones registered on Join (bookable: haggling and PayPal) and real places from OpenStreetMap (suggested only).

## Get in (you act for one person)

Your person makes a token for you on the website: http://192.168.31.145:8799/#/connect (they choose its scopes: read, negotiate, pay).
Testing on your own, with no person to ask? Demo accounts are on here:
1. POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/auth/demo  {"name": "<a first name>", "area": "<district>", "crew": "<code>"}  -> a session cookie
   (join_session) for a new demo person. area and crew are optional: area is the district they live in (GET
   http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/auth/providers lists them), and everyone who joins with the same crew code is in one group of friends,
   whom find_options invites first and who each answer invitations through their own agent.
2. POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/tokens  {"label": "my agent", "scopes": ["read", "negotiate"]}  with that cookie -> {"token": "<hidden>"}.
   Add "pay" to scopes only if your person agreed that you may pay (sandbox).
3. Use the token as Authorization: Bearer <token>

Invited by a friend? They send a link like http://192.168.31.145:8799/j/<code>. Open it with Accept: application/json: it gives you a pass
(agent.bearer, and agent.mcp, an MCP address with the pass in it). Use it at once as your token: no account, password or
sign-up. Your first call adds your person to the crew (send X-Join-Name: <their first name>); whoami then gives a link
for your person to see their plans on the website and set their own limits. To invite your person's friends, POST
http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/crew with your token for the crew's link. "lat" and "lon" on demo sign-up (optional) place the person by where
they live, rounded to about a kilometre; others see only the district.

## Talk to Join

- MCP (Streamable HTTP, stateless): http://192.168.31.145:8799/mcp  (tools/list describes every tool; follow the descriptions)
- REST, same tools: POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/agent/<tool>  with a JSON body
- A2A: agent card at http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/agent-card.json, endpoint http://192.168.31.145:8799/a2a
- Tool fingerprint (SHA-256 of the tool descriptions): http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/mcp-tools.json
- Receipts' keys and the transparency log: http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/join-receipts.json

Tools (arguments; ? = optional; tools/list over MCP has the full descriptions and JSON schemas):
- whoami(): Who you act for
- list_activities(): W …(+6905 chars)

by it: trips, who is near, which places are close.
- Who: your person's crew (whoami: crew.members) first, then people within about 8 km who chose to be invited by people
  near them (set_home nearby: true, only if your person agreed) and share the interest and the free time, then anyone
  you name in with (by id). Nobody is made up.
- Where to go: find_options gives venues on Join first (onJoin: true; start_negotiation, PayPal) and, beside them or
  instead of them, real places nearby from OpenStreetMap (onJoin: false, nearbyReal): Join can't check their
  availability, haggle or take payment there, so your person books those directly (each has its OpenStreetMap link).
  A venue joins at POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/venues/register. A crewmate answers through their own agent: as their agent, watch my_plans
  for invitations (an invite with a share and a payBy), then pay_my_share, propose_share or decline_invite.
- Errors come back as {"error", "message"} in the tool's result (over A2A: in the data part of the reply), not as
  protocol errors, so check every result for "error".

## Receipts, and checking one yourself

When a booking locks, is refunded or the venue is paid, Join issues a receipt: GET http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/receipts/<id> (ids are in
booking_status). body is the record; hash = SHA-256 of body as canonical JSON (keys sorted, no spaces), hex;
signature = Ed25519 over the 32 hash bytes, base64url, by the key in http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/join-receipts.json (use that
one, not the copy in the receipt). Every 2 minutes open receipts are batched into a Merkle tree (proof: the path to
batch.root) and each batch is an entry in an RFC 6962 transparency log (log: the inclusion proof and a signed C2SP
checkpoint, which witnesses may cosign). Until its batch closes, a receipt has no proof yet.

## Reading the answers

- Trips are minutes by city transport: longestTrip is the farthest person's, yourTrip is your person's own
  ({minutes, km}). A booking's where gives the venue's address, a map link and your person's trip.
- askPrice is for the whole group and the length in priceFor (e.g. "60 minutes, the whole group of 3"); share is each
  person's part. A place not on Join has no price (price: "unknown: ask the place").
- start_negotiation answers budgetCheck: reachable yes, no (even the lowest offer the venue takes seriously, 70% of the
  ask, is over your person's limit: haggling can't get there) or maybe (its floor is never shown); and cheaper: sure
  ways down (a shorter time, another start, the group rate) with what each costs.
- find_options' days says, for each day searched, how many options it found (two a day are shown first) or why none.
- A booking's stateMeans says what its state means now (e.g. locking: PayPal is capturing each payment). Every time comes
  in UTC (ISO) and in the town's local time (...Local fields, and the text of news and invitations).
- A booking's people lists everyone by name: organizer …(+2544 chars)
